question: Which ECG finding meets the diagnostic threshold for STEMI in leads V2–V3 in a 45-year-old male?

answers.text: New ST elevation ≥1 mm in V2 and V3

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The threshold for V2–V3 is higher than limb leads. ≥1 mm meets criteria in limb leads and V4–V6, but not V2–V3 in men under 40.

answers.text: New ST elevation ≥2 mm in V2 and V3

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. STEMI criteria in V2–V3 require ≥2 mm (0.2 mV) ST elevation in men ≥40 years; ≥2.5 mm in men <40. This threshold is higher than the ≥1 mm criterion used for other leads.

answers.text: New ST elevation ≥0.5 mm in V2 and V3

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 0.5 mm ST elevation does not meet STEMI criteria in any lead. This threshold is used for posterior leads in some guidelines.

answers.text: New T-wave inversion in V2 and V3

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: New T-wave inversion in V2–V3 may suggest posterior MI or anterior ischaemia but does not constitute a STEMI pattern.

overallFeedback.feedback: STEMI ECG criteria: ≥1 mm ST elevation in ≥2 contiguous limb leads or V4–V6; ≥2 mm in V2–V3 (men ≥40); ≥2.5 mm in V2–V3 (men <40); ≥1.5 mm in V2–V3 (women).
Well done. The ≥2 mm threshold in V2–V3 for men ≥40 is a standard STEMI criterion that must be memorised — this is the lead pair with the highest threshold.
